Text-reuse calculations from DharmaNexus identify 696 matching passages shared between the *Dānakathā* and 53 other Pali works [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records substantial internal reuse within the *Kathāvatthu* itself, including debates such as the *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1), *Kukkuḷakathā* (Kv 2.8), *Sīlaṁacetasikantikathā* (Kv 10.7), *Rūpaṁkammantikathā* (Kv 8.9), *Sabbamatthītikathā* (Kv 1.6), and the preceding *Cetasikakathā* (Kv 7.3), as well as matches in the *Sikkhāpadavibhaṅga* (Vb 14) and the *Sīlakkhandhavaggaṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Across corpora, DharmaNexus aligns passages of the text with the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu* (best score 85, aligning §7.7) and Tibetan canonical texts such as the *Ārya-satpuruṣa-sūtra* (D0327, 19 matches, best score 65) and the *Dhātubahuka-sūtra* (D0297) [DharmaNexus].

No substantive discussion of this specific *Kathāvatthu* section appears in the secondary literature passages provided, as all matched records represent substring false positives referring to the *Nidānakathā* of the Jātaka commentary.
